facts.text: I discuss how mathematics was treated within Christian philosophy.
Augustine wrote De Libero Arbitrio (On free choice of the will) between 387 and 395.
Augustine compared knowledge of arithmetica to divine revelation in De Libero Arbitrio.
Boethius translated books by Aristotle and Plato.
Computus was used to calculate the day of Easter.
The Council of Nicaea in 325 agreed that Easter would be on the first Sunday after the first full moon in spring.
The Pandectae is described as a Latin adaptation of πανδέκτης meaning “covering everything”.
The Pandectae contained verdicts on inheritance that used numbers.
During the Carolingian renaissance, around 800 AD, a new codification of the corpus of Christian knowledge was called for.
Children of the new aristocracy were supposed to be educated in the Artes liberales.
The Artes liberales were subdivided into the trivium and quadrivium.
The trivium consisted of grammar, rhetorics, and dialectics.
The quadrivium consisted of arithmetica, musica, geometria, and astronomia.

events.text: Augustine wrote De Libero Arbitrio (On free choice of the will).
Council of Nicaea agreed on the rule for Easter timing.
Carolingian renaissance called for a new codification of Christian knowledge.
